text: dsh-memu-memory 为 DSH Web 客户端提供本地优先的对话记忆，适合长篇角色扮演与陪伴聊天。它在会话步骤中注入相关记忆，并注册记忆读写工具与 MemU 设置界面。功能包括私有记忆的分层保存和召回、来源与可见范围管理、记忆关系图、词典查询以及图片记忆管理。适合希望角色跨回合记住事实并能在界面中整理记忆的用户。默认使用本地 JSON 索引和词法召回；向量引擎及外部模型端点可按需配置。

dsh-memu-memory adds local-first memory to DSH web chats. It injects relevant memories during sessions and provides tools plus a settings UI to manage layered memories, recall, links, and a lexicon. The default uses a local JSON index with lexical recall; vector search is optional.
想让 DSH 角色在长对话里记住之前提过的重要事实。
有没有办法给每段会话保存可检索的私人记忆？
希望 AI 能按当前聊天内容自动找回相关记忆。
我想查看、编辑和整理角色积累下来的记忆。
能不能把记忆之间的人物和事件关系可视化？
想按来源和可见范围区分记忆，避免混淆角色知道的内容。
I want my DSH character to remember important facts across long chats.
Can the assistant retrieve relevant memories automatically during a conversation?
**dsh-memu-memory** 的功能「分层记忆与自动召回」：它把私有记忆写入索引，并在会话步骤中注入与当前对话相关的内容；记忆可分长期、短期和必须记住等层。 可通过会话自动流程或插件界面使用。
**dsh-memu-memory** 的功能「记忆图谱」：它提供记忆与实体的关联能力，可记录关系证据并供界面查看关联结构。 可通过会话自动流程或插件界面使用。
**dsh-memu-memory** 的功能「记忆管理界面」：它提供 MemU 页面，用于浏览、编辑和整理记忆及相关设置。 可通过会话自动流程或插件界面使用。
**dsh-memu-memory** 的功能「词典与术语检索」：它支持在当前对话可见的词典范围内搜索活跃术语，并可管理私有词典内容。 可通过会话自动流程或插件界面使用。

dsh-memu-memory README · Introduction：

dsh-memu-memory

A local-first memory plugin for DeepSeek Harness — shared by folder, bound to a chat, written by the agent, curated in the background, and honest about what it does not know.
dsh-memu-memory README · Introduction：

dsh-memu-memory README · Introduction：`dsh-memu-memory` is built for long-form RP and companion chats. It gives a DSH conversation a memory that behaves like memory instead of a log: three retention layers that fade, a first-turn anchor plus at most one per-turn recall, provenance that cannot be quietly upgraded from "I inferred it" to "they said it", contradictions that wait for a decision instead of both being read as true, near-identical facts collapse to one entry and one recall seat, and an optional relationship graph with evidence. Speakers, characters, worlds and story branches form hard boundaries, and what a character is allowed to know stays separate from what actually happened.

dsh-memu-memory README · Introduction：It is **local-first by default**. The default `agent` backend stores full text in JSON indexes and recalls lexically — no Python, no embedding service, no API key. The `api` backend switches recall to the optional, pinned MemU engine (vector search). MemU is a plugin for people who want it, not a requirement for the plugin to start.

dsh-memu-memory README · Introduction：> [!WARNING]
> **Early-stage software.** This plugin is still early and may contain unforeseen errors, bugs or breaking changes. Back up your data, and please [report an issue](https://github.com/Tkingxiao/dsh-memu-memory/issues) or send a pull request — feedback helps the project improve.

dsh-memu-memory README · What it remembers：- **Three layers, one timeline.** `short_term` drafts expire after 72 hours by default; `long_term` is the body of ordinary memory; `must_remember` needs a reason and a source, decays over 365 days with a 0.35 strength floor, and can be *marginalized* but never auto-deleted to make room.
- **Recall is a moment, not a dump.** The first turn after a session starts (or after compaction) gets an anchor block with budgets for pinned, core and global memory. After that, each user turn gets at most one recall. Deduplication and a token budget are enforced in code, not left to the prompt. Anchor and recall entries are **title cards**: title, id and semantic tags only. The body stays in the drawer and behind `memu_private_recall` / `memu_global_recall`, so the same budget exposes far more memories without pasting text the model never asked for.
- **A private lexicon writes itself.** The consolidation worker extracts stable, evidenced slang, memes and project terms with one term per entry. Ordinary entries become active immediately (no human review queue), while sensitive triggers and sensitive edits stay user-only. The lexicon page is a card flow w

dsh-memu-memory README · Active memory, measured：Idle consolidation is not "every quiet session gets a fork". Before a fork the plugin scores the evidence since the last cursor: human turns (`H`), content volume (`C`: human text, assistant text and deduped successful tool results, 2,000 characters per result) and effective tool work units (`U`), with `score = 0.35*min(H/3,2) + 0.45*min(C/4000,2) + 0.20*min(U/20,2)` (default threshold 0.8). A session idle for 15 minutes wakes below that score only when it is small; transcripts of 2,000+ events must earn their fork, because the host seeds the full prefix. A recent consolidation or a recent recall suppresses the idle fork.

dsh-memu-memory README · Active memory, measured：More is not better: thin turns on a large transcript are skipped by the guard (about 37% fewer prompt tokens on the same scenarios, at the cost of roughly 1 in 22 labels arriving a little later), but once the unconsolidated range passes 600 events the check runs unconditionally, so decisions made early in a long session do not stay out of memory forever.

Four real long sessions from this machine were replayed read-only (no new chat) and their turns were counted:

dsh-memu-memory README · Active memory, measured：| Session | Events | Turns | Score-qualified | Below threshold | Fresh human turns after cursor |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `62056bff…` | 5,913 | 12 | 6 | 6 | 0 |
| `adedb9ac…` | 5,766 | 23 | 16 | 7 | 0 |
| `e38a0de0…` | 85 | 2 | 0 | 2 | 0 |
| `edf7dc5c…` | 78 | 4 | 0 | 4 | 0 |

dsh-memu-memory README · Active memory, measured：Below-threshold turns on the two small sessions can still wake through starvation; on the 2,000+ event sessions they do not. None of the four had new human input after its real cursor, so none would fork again immediately.

Provider-reported usage from real forks: one consolidation costs about **41k–217k input tokens** (including cache reads; it depends on memory-tool steps) and **0.8k–3.4k output**. At one 4-hour long session per day and 2–6 effective consolidations:

dsh-memu-memory README · Active memory, measured：| Consolidations/day | Monthly input | Monthly output |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2 | ~5.6M | ~0.11M |
| 4 | ~11M | ~0.23M |
| 6 | ~17M | ~0.34M |
| 6 (worst measured fork each) | ~39M | ~0.7M |

dsh-memu-memory README · Active memory, measured：For scale, the whole 4-hour session tree measured here consumed 132M input and 1.28M output in one day, so active-memory forks are about **0.2%–1%** of the total. These are token counts, not money; cache reads are usually billed at a lower rate. The exact figure depends on turn count, memory-tool steps and how often the session actually goes idle.

dsh-memu-memory README · One WebUI：The sidebar has exactly **one** entry: **MemU WebUI**. The memory wall and all settings live in the same navigation, with deep links such as `#/settings/memories`, `#/settings/folders` and `#/settings/stats`. The interface follows the browser locale (Chinese or English).

dsh-memu-memory README · One WebUI：**Private / global groups with multi-select.** The "Memories" page splits into **Private** and **Global** blocks (private first, default). The private block supports **multi-select**: bulk archive, restore and permanent delete (two-step confirm) — one failed row never eats the rest. Every row on the Global memory page has a "View" action that jumps straight to that entry on the wall.

dsh-memu-memory README · One WebUI：**In-place work.** Clicking a memory card opens a right-side drawer with the full text and the fields that decide how it behaves — title, content, tags, disclosure, confidence, open loop — plus save, archive, restore and "open in the browser" for heavier work. Archived memories can be deleted in the same drawer; the first click only arms it and the second confirms. Global memories are read-only in the drawer and link to their own page. Filters and scroll position stay where they were. Cards that carry images use the first usable attachment as a cover, and the drawer opens the full gallery; `secret` and `never_say` entries never receive a pixel URL, so they show a label instead.

dsh-memu-memory README · One WebUI：**Graph and list together.** The **Relations** tab renders the graph canvas and the adjacency list side by side (stacked on narrow screens), with the focus selector above them and link/entity/relationship tools below. There is no mode switch to forget. The scope selector also carries a **Global memory** entry: nodes are global entries and edges are `related/refines/supports`; the global view is read-only, and edges are removed from the global memory list.

dsh-memu-memory README · One WebUI：The locally bundled D3 force layout preserves positions and the camera across background data refreshes. Drag nodes, pan the background, zoom with the wheel or pinch, fit the graph, and highlight neighbors. Labels avoid collisions; graph settings adjust repulsion, link distance, labels and live layout. Layout only visualizes recorded links: it never infers or writes relationships. The graph page also lists **entity merge candidates** (same kind, contained or near-identical spellings) — suggestions only, confirmed by two clicks, and merging redirects links and folds aliases into the main node without deleting any memory.

dsh-memu-memory README · One WebUI：| Page | What it is for |
|---|---|
| Memories | Private/global grouped wall, source/status/library/preview, in-place drawer, multi-select bulk ops, node graph tab |
| Engine & connection | Optional MemU engine install/switch, embedding endpoint, backups and restore; local runtime download shows MB/s, offers npmjs / npmmirror, and supports pause, stop and resume |
| Memory settings | Injection mode, token budgets, topK, same-domain cross-library recall, relevance threshold, retention, open-loop cadence, freshness hint, date wake-up, automation |
| Folders | Folder-level private/global ceiling, expandable conversations and their own switches |
| Libraries | Create, rename, archive, restore, explicitly delete libraries |
| Memory browser | Full-text editing, attachments, review queue, graph and bounded canvas, JSON/ZIP import/export |
| Global memory | Domain-scoped global memories, evidence, review queue and the separate curator; every row can jump to the wall |
| Prompts | General / RP / Coding / Mixed variants, overrides and per-key reset; new conversations start on RP and can pick a domain in the first-run prompt |
| Stats | Daily activity, hit

dsh-memu-memory README · One WebUI：Settings save as you change them (250 ms debounce), with about 2.5 s cross-window sync and a heartbeat for writes made by tools or another window. The WebUI opens in a new tab; when a popup is blocked it falls back to an in-app overlay without unloading the host SPA. Light, dark, reduced-motion and narrow layouts are supported.

dsh-memu-memory README · Injection token budgets：`anchorTokens` and `turnTokens` bound anchor and recall content independently (default 800 each). `injectionTotalTokens` caps the whole plugin message (default 2000); it does not replace the recall budget. Title cards spend far fewer tokens per entry than full text, so the same budget exposes more memories; the budget itself was deliberately not increased in 1.2.2.

dsh-memu-memory README · Time-sensitive memory (1.2.3)：- **Stale recall says so.** When recalled entries carry a time signal (a one-off date already in the past, wording like "latest / current / price / version", or an entry older than `freshnessDays`), one conditional line is appended after the recall block telling the model to verify with a search tool *if the conversation has one*. It never claims a tool exists, and it is dropped rather than pushing recall over budget.
- **Dated promises keep asking.** An `open_loop` memory whose `YYYY-MM-DD` has passed is re-raised every `openLoopRemindDays` (default 7) with its date and how late it is — undated promises keep the old "quiet after one mention" behaviour. Closing a loop is always the user's action.
- **Optional wake-up call.** `salientWake` (default **off**) schedules a one-shot host task per bound conversation so a salient date is spoken about on the day, even if the conversation went cold. The delivered turn carries its own text — recall and anniversary blocks do not run there — and the tasks are visible in the host's schedule UI. Requires the host process to be running; experimental until verified on a real install.

dsh-memu-memory README · Domain Prompts：Resident guidance, writing policies and consolidation prompts follow the current session domain. Local tools and remote JSON consolidation share the domain body, with separate supported output contracts. New conversations default to RP; Coding, Mixed and custom pages stay enabled and can be selected per conversation. The new-conversation memory prompt also offers the four memory domains, so a coding session can be started in an RP workspace without remembering to change the sidebar afterwards.

dsh-memu-memory README · Domain Prompts：| Domain | Memory focus |
|---|---|
| Coding | Requirements, acceptance criteria, interfaces, call chains, invariants, root causes, tradeoffs, verification and handoff points. Neutral engineering notes, not character psychology. Preserve necessary minimal code and exact semantics without copying whole files or truncating critical conditions. |
| RP | Evidenced moments, character reactions, names and habits, commitments, boundaries and repair. Let memory shape present choices without repetitive callbacks, invented facts or automatic intimacy. |
| Mixed | The prompt separates technical, character and OOC material per item; it does not automatically change the session domain. Tags aid retrieval, not access control or character knowledge. |
| General | Neutral facts, preferences, decisions with reasons, promises and constraints; no default roleplay. |

dsh-memu-memory README · Domain Prompts：Updated defaults never overwrite custom text. The default-update notice remains until that prompt is saved or reset. Compare, merge or restore individual prompts in **Prompts**; there is no need to clear memories. Regression tests cover routing and output contracts, not a guarantee of naturalness or long-term memory quality, which still requires real-conversation evaluation.

dsh-memu-memory README · Method 1 — npm (recommended)：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-memu-memory
dsh web
```

Restart the host after installing or updating. The plugin appears as **Settings → MemU**, and the right sidebar gets the **MemU WebUI** button.

> Replace `web` with your profile name if you use another one. Older DSH CLIs accept the shorter form `dsh plugin add dsh-memu-memory` without the profile flag.

dsh-memu-memory README · Method 2 — npx (no global install)：```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-memu-memory
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
```

dsh-memu-memory README · Method 3 — from a local checkout (development)：The repository has **no build step**: `lib/` is the runtime. Clone it, link the checkout into your DSH profile, and add the bundle.

```sh
git clone <this repository> dsh-memu-memory
cd dsh-memu-memory
npm ci --legacy-peer-deps
```

In the profile's `package.json`:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "dsh-memu-memory": "link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-memu-memory"
  },

Then restart DSH. A symlinked checkout is picked up on restart; there is no bundle cache.

dsh-memu-memory README · Optional — vector engine (MemU)：The default `agent` backend is fully usable without this step. Install the engine from **Settings → MemU → Engine & connection**, or from a terminal:

```sh
npx --package dsh-memu-memory dsh-memu-memory-setup
```

What it does:

dsh-memu-memory README · Optional — vector engine (MemU)：The default `memoryBackend="agent"` uses lexical recall and does not call an embedding service. To enable the vector library, choose `memoryBackend="api"`, then select `vectorSource="local"` for managed local embeddings or `vectorSource="api"` for a configured compatible embedding endpoint (which may itself run on localhost). Both sources feed MemU storage and retrieval; installing the MemU engine alone does not enable vectors.

dsh-memu-memory README · Optional — vector engine (MemU)：`memoryMode` (`local` / `cloud`) is a MemU storage-compatibility setting, not the embedding switch or source selector; its cloud option is not a claim that managed local inference is offline cloud storage. Summary generation is configured independently of the vector route: ordinary private consolidation uses an Agent fork; an explicit remote-summary action uses its chat endpoint and commits through the same memory write path. Recall uses neither LLM reranking nor an LLM fallback. Exact memory ids still use the direct path; the plugin does not maintain a parallel vector database.

dsh-memu-memory README · Optional — vector engine (MemU)：Managed model download, progress reporting and profile-switch/migration flows are implemented, but real model/runtime downloads and end-to-end native inference/switching have not been verified in this work. A candidate or `pending` artifact is not available for use; it must not be advertised as downloadable or ready until its artifact and validation gates pass.

dsh-memu-memory README · First run：1. Install, then restart DSH.
2. Open **MemU WebUI** from the sidebar (or Settings → MemU).
3. New conversations ask once whether this chat should use memory: private only, global only, both, or none. **Remember my choice** skips the question later. The card you pick **sets both switches at once**, so the sidebar shows the card you chose; the advanced "existing / new library" pick only changes which library the private layer reads, never the two switches.
4. If you want a folder-wide ceiling, set it under **文件夹** — a folder can forbid private or global memory, and the chat switches will respect that ceiling.
5. Talk. The agent writes private memories itself. The **MemU 记忆** wall is where you review, edit, archive, link and export them.

dsh-memu-memory README · First run：Folder policy is a **ceiling, not an initial value**: turning a folder switch off immediately clamps every conversation in it, and turning it back on restores each conversation's own choice. A folder with both switches off does not prompt, does not create a library and does not inject anything.

dsh-memu-memory README · Model tools：| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `memu_private_remember` | Write a private memory, with source, layer, disclosure, visibility, tags, open loop and attachment references |
| `memu_private_recall` | Natural-language or exact-id recall; results may carry up to two relationship pointers |
| `memu_private_list` | List the memories usable in the current scope |
| `memu_private_update` | Edit, without bypassing pin admission, review or visibility rules |
| `memu_private_archive` | Archive; never delete |
| `memu_private_unpin` | Marginalize a permanent memory with a first-person reason, quota and cooldown |
| `memu_private_link` | Link memories/entities with evidence, or update a relationship snapshot; also adjudicates `memu_private_link_suggest` candidates; cannot delete edges |
| `memu_private_link_suggest` | Run the local high-confidence linking/entity-hub pass for ids written this consolidation and return only uncertain candidate pairs |
| `memu_lexicon_search` | Search active lexicon terms this conversation can see: bound library + global lexicon (+ same-domain libraries when cross-library recall is on); archived and tombstoned terms stay hidden |
|
dsh-memu-memory README · Model tools：The main agent has **no global write tool**. Global memories are produced only by the separate curator.

dsh-memu-memory README · Privacy, permissions & data：**What is stored.** Everything lives under `~/.dsh/dsh-memu-memory/` (or `$DSH_MEMU_MEMORY_HOME`; the legacy `$DSH_MEMU_HOME` and `~/.dsh/dsh-memu` are still honoured when no new `state.json` exists):

```text
~/.dsh/dsh-memu-memory/
├─ state.json                 settings, folder policies, session bindings
├─ index/<libraryId>.json     private memory bodies (source of truth)
├─ index/global.json          global memories

dsh-memu-memory README · Privacy, permissions & data：- **Text and images are not encrypted at rest.** The directory is inside your home directory. If that is not acceptable, do not store secrets in memories and protect the disk with OS-level encryption.
- **Images are opt-in privacy data.** Only host-approved attachments are captured. `secret` entries never serve their attachments over the HTTP route; `never_say` captions are not echoed. The vision description service is enabled by default, but it only sends an image after you configure an endpoint, and it may cost money. It never uses host credentials automatically.
- **Network.** No telemetry. Outbound traffic happens only for (a) the optional engine installer downloading Python packages/uv from the configured mirrors, (b) the embedding endpoint you configure, (c) the optional remote summary model, and (d) the vision endpoint you configure (enabled by default; no call is made until an endpoint is configured). The default backend makes no external calls for memory operations.
- **Shell and filesystem.** The optional engine installer uses Python/pip in a private venv (and a pinned uv fallback inside the plugin directory). It does n

dsh-memu-memory README · External messages in a long tool turn：A host turn may remain open while a third-party tool waits for messages.
New human input can trigger one bounded recall at the next model step without
ending that turn or making another model call. Native user messages work directly.
Unmarked tool logs, sleep completions, failed calls and empty polls do not trigger it.
The plugin does not depend on a particular waiting implementation.

dsh-memu-memory README · External messages in a long tool turn：The channel/character/world/branch must match the conversation's configured memory
scope; omit unavailable identities rather than guessing them. Images must use
`{ type: 'image', attachment: hostAdmittedRef }`, never filesystem paths, URLs or bytes.
If metadata is unavailable, return the complete protocol as JSON text and list
the exact tool name under **External message tool allowlist**. JSON embedded in logs
or code fences is not accepted, nor is JSON from an unapproved tool.

dsh-memu-memory README · External messages in a long tool turn：An in-process integration may instead import
`ingestInboundBatch` from `dsh-memu-memory/integration` and call
`ingestInboundBatch({ sessionId, batch, ctx, session })`. It registers work only:
the producer still delivers the actual incoming content to the model. It does not
wake the agent, append a fake user turn or write fact memories.
section: External messages in a long tool turn

dsh-memu-memory README · External messages in a long tool turn：Deduplication uses producer + channel + speaker + message id; changing a delivery id
does not replay an already processed message. Memory cadence advances by human-message
batches even when the host turn number stays fixed. Pending input is capped at 32
messages / eight images / 96 KB, with at most 4000 characters per external text block;
overflow is explicitly refused, never silently discarded. Split oversized batches.
Recall failure preserves the queue with a 30-second retry delay; cancellation does not consume it.
Only the admitted batch is confirmed, so messages arriving during recall remain pending.
Running agents (including waiting tools) and pending batches are not sleep-consolidated;
the idle window starts from real message activity or the agent's return to idle.
`memu_status` reports `inbound` queue/clock/result and `inbound_error` when degraded.

dsh-memu-memory README · Compatibility & limits：- **Host:** DSH `>=0.2.0-rc.1`, using public extension points only (tools, injection, session query, subagents, slots, a prefixed HTTP route). No host source modifications. The core surfaces (13 `memu_*` tools, guide injection, settings page, right-sidebar tab, prefixed RPC) were verified on `0.2.2-rc.1` on 2026-11-05; the check table lives in [`docs/host-adaptation.md`](docs/host-adaptation.md). The optional dated-wake feature uses the host-wide `ctx.schedule` task API introduced in `0.2.2`; on `0.2.0`–`0.2.1` (session-scoped reminders) it detects the older shape and skips with one warning instead of retrying every sweep.
- **Recall quality:** the default backend is lexical. Semantic recall depends on the optional engine and the embedding model you choose; the plugin cannot improve a model it does not own. LongMemEval, long-running group-chat A/B and "human-likeness" scores have **not** been run — test counts are not a quality score.
- **No cloud sync, no accounts, no cross-device sync.** This is a local plugin with no server-side identity.

npm ci --legacy-peer-deps
npm test                                  # full suite; the isolated real-engine case skips unless configured
npm run check                             # syntax + i18n key alignment + package.json

dsh-memu-memory README · Development & verification：With the preview running, use `npm run test:graph-browser -- http://127.0.0.1:7789/dsh-memu-memory/ui#/settings/memories` in another terminal to check 200 nodes, desktop/narrow layouts, dragging, refresh stability, themes and load retries. Run `npx playwright install chromium` once, or set `GRAPH_BROWSER_CHANNEL=msedge` on Windows to use installed Edge. Stress data is intercepted only in the test browser and never written to memory. No CDN is needed at runtime; bundled D3 licenses are in `lib/webui/graph-LICENSE.txt`.

dsh-memu-memory README · Development & verification：The suite includes two optional real-engine integration cases: curator writing requires `DSH_MEMU_TEST_ENGINE_PYTHON`, and the backup venv/WAL case requires `DSH_MEMU_BACKUP_REAL_ENGINE=1`; both are skipped by default. The 50 automated acceptance checks pass. The optional engine was installed and smoke-tested in an isolated directory with the pinned wheel; embedding tests use a local deterministic server, which proves the protocol, not semantic quality.
